configuration: AiGet full pipeline (variant 'aiget'): the Gemini-based prototype used in the in-lab and real-world studies, i.e. mixed-initiative LLM request trigger (gaze fixation, 12 s timer plus FPV-difference check, ring-mouse verbal query), Context Analysis Agent prompted with the participant-provided user profile and gaze-pattern/familiarity rules, Knowledge Generation Agent with focus/familiarity rules, the Novelty x (Align + Utility + Unexpectedness) scoring, the suggestion-history filter (10 most relevant history items injected, candidates with similarity >= 0.75 to history dropped), and two parallel output-transformation agents (emoji/text/audio rendering and entity bounding-box localisation). In code this is get_llm_response(pipeline='AiGet') driven by PANDAExpFrontend (mode='Glasses', auto=True) at commit 92b17f8. The ablation baselines (paper: w/o R, w/o RP; code: Baseline_w_o_S, knowledge_generation_wo_sp) were not judged.

S->M.label: reported
S->M.rationale: The code retains interpreted sensed evidence across requests: after every response, Frontend.process_response stores the Context Analysis Agent's 'Context Description' (its interpretation of the FPV frames with gaze, time and location) in last_ai_response next to the delivered suggestion, and on the next user-initiated request this retained record is appended to the context-analysis input as 'Previous AI Response' so that a follow-up question can be resolved against the previous moment (context_description prompt step 5). Retention scope is one step (overwritten per response) within a running session. The participant-provided profile is a static file written before the study and does not itself establish a write path, and the spoken question is only inserted into the current request, not stored. The paper describes compiling user query transcriptions per request and supporting follow-up questions but does not itself describe retaining the context description, so this channel rests on the code read alongside the text.

M->A.label: reported
M->A.rationale: Retained information drives content and silence decisions. (a) The suggestion history (AI_suggestion_history, in memory for the session, optionally seeded from data/recordings/<pid>/ai_suggestions.json at start-up) is reduced to the 10 items most similar to the current context description and injected into the knowledge-generation request as 'Suggestion History (*avoid similar content in the following list*)'; after generation every Live Comments item with cosine similarity >= 0.75 to history is dropped, and if nothing survives get_llm_response returns no location and the Frontend only logs, so the service stays silent. (b) The participant-provided profile is inserted into the knowledge-generation instruction whose rules set knowledge type and depth by familiarity and interests and retain only items scoring >= 2. (c) last_ai_response is supplied to answer follow-up questions. The paper states the same mechanism in Sec 5.1.3 and Table 2.

A->S.label: reported
A->S.rationale: Two in-system flows from Action to Sensing. (1) After the Knowledge Generation Agent selects the suggestion, a parallel output-transformation agent receives the chosen suggestion text plus the primary/peripheral entity names and is instructed to find, in the FPV frame sequence, the frame number and relative xyxy box of the mentioned entity; the Frontend then displays that frame with the box. The action content thus sets the target of a new interpretation of the sensed frames; the paper states the bounding-box image reference and the two parallel agents in Sec 5.1.4. (2) Execution state gates acquisition: the frames sent with the last request are kept as last_sent_video_sequence_queue and the Backend continuously compares the current frame queue with them (MobileNet embeddings, similarity threshold 0.6) so a new context analysis is only triggered when the scene has changed since the last request, and no_other_request_running() suppresses triggers while a request, a voice recording or audio playback is in progress; the paper states the FPV-difference condition in Sec 5.1.1.

M->S.label: reported
M->S.rationale: Retained priors are supplied to the Context Analysis Agent, which is the Sensing interpreter: the user profile is inserted into the context_description system instruction, which tells the model to judge whether the environment and entities are familiar from the profile, to use the profile to find unnoticed peripheral entities aligned with the user's interests, and to predict familiar entities from it; the paper states in Sec 5.1.2 that the profile is used during context analysis to assess familiarity and link the scene to interests, and that the agent analyses 'short-term attention and long-term interests'. In addition the retained last response (last suggestion plus last context description) is given to the context-analysis step when the user asks a question so the agent decides whether the question refers to the previous moment. This is a direct supply of retained information to interpretation, not merely an Action decision that requests a new observation. The profile being static (participant-provided) does not affect a read path.

Cross-session seeding from ai_suggestions.json is loaded at start-up, but that file is produced by a script absent from the repository, so the retention scope established by the released code is the running session.

notes: Judged the full AiGet pipeline as run in the studies (v2, 24 Feb 2025). Source access limits: WebFetch truncated the arXiv HTML at Sec 5.3 and ar5iv at Sec 6.3; all PDF copies exceed the fetch size limit and ACM/ResearchGate are blocked, so Sec 6.4-9 and the appendices were not read verbatim (search summaries only: post-session questionnaires and interviews; Limitations on latency, hallucination and privacy; all UNVERIFIED). Two early broad fetches returned fabricated text for Sec 6-8 (two contradictory 'Limitations' sections) and were discarded. All paper quotes above came through the WebFetch summarizer; each cited sentence was matched word-for-word across at least two independent extractions (arXiv HTML and ar5iv) but could not be checked against the raw page. Code quotes are verbatim from the checked-out commit. Code/paper discrepancies: main.py uses gemini-1.5-flash for knowledge generation and LLMPipeline uses gemini-2.0-flash-exp for context analysis, whereas the paper reports Gemini-1.5-Flash for context analysis/output transformation and Gemini-1.5-Pro for knowledge generation. Quirk: Frontend only passes the history list once last_ai_response is set, so a loaded ai_suggestions.json is not used on the very first request of a session.
